task.instructions:
Using matplotlib, read cases.csv (columns: district, year, cases) and population.csv (columns: district, population_thousands — population in THOUSANDS of people). Compute each district's 2023 case rate per 100,000 residents and draw it as a horizontal bar chart.
Requirements:
- Use only 2023 cases.
- Omit any district that has no entry in population.csv.
- Sort the bars so the highest rate is at the top.
- Draw a vertical black dashed line at the overall 2023 rate across the plotted districts (total cases divided by total population, per 100,000).
- Label the x axis 'Cases per 100,000 residents (2023)'.
- Give the chart a title.
- Make the figure 9 by 6 inches.
Save the figure as figure.png.

function.arguments: {"command": "python3 -c \"import pandas as pd; import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; cases_df = pd.read_csv('cases.csv'); population_df = pd.read_csv('population.csv'); combined_df = cases_df.merge(population_df, on='district', how='left'); combined_df['case_rate'] = combined_df['cases'] * 100000 / combined_df['population_thousands']; combined_df = combined_df[combined_df['year'] == 2023]; combined_df = combined_df.dropna(subset=['population_thousands']); combined_df.sort_values(by='case_rate', ascending=False, inplace=True); plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6)); plt.barh(combined_df['district'], combined_df['case_rate'], color='blue'); plt.axvline(x=combined_df['case_rate'].mean(), linestyle='--', color='black'); plt.xlabel('Cases per 100,000 residents (2023)'); plt.title('District Case Rates in 2023'); plt.savefig('figure.png'); plt.show()\""}
function.name: bash
